children: A single Go binary that terminates TLS once and routes every public path on the box to the right backend.

Caddy is the front door on Production: one statically-linked Go binary holding a single ACME certificate for api.barkpark.cloud. It fronts two upstreams — the Phoenix API on :4000 and the Indx Engine on :5001 — using handle blocks that match by path. /studio reaches LiveView Studio, /indx reaches the retriever seam, and /papers reaches the Bulldocs reader; everything else falls through to Phoenix.

Caddy exists to own HTTPS so the app doesn't try to. Earlier, Phoenix set force_ssl, which redirected http://<ip> to https:// when no HTTPS terminator existed — an infinite 301 loop that returned empty bodies for every API call. Pushing TLS termination out to Caddy and leaving force_ssl off cured it. Caddy also keeps answering on its cached cert during a Deploy, so the 60–90s systemd Service restart is invisible to external callers.

Because Caddy presents https://api.barkpark.cloud to the browser, Phoenix's check_origin must whitelist that exact host with PHX_SCHEME=https. When the baked-in origin drifted to the raw IP, the /live/websocket upgrade returned 403 and LiveView Studio went click-dead. The handle blocks therefore route, but the env must agree. Webhooks callbacks and HTTP API v1 traffic all enter through this same binary.
